TDN.Requirements.Msc.msc_security_level_: The credential rules prevent Inner components at different security levels from authenticating. Selected management devices are also separated by level. The modeled set of established tunnels must agree with the authentication rules.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.key_and_management_: Finite credential, manager and pair records are checked. A general argument shows that a credential or manager cannot belong to two different levels under those assignments. The conclusion covers every clause of the accepted specification under the theorem’s explicit assumptions.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.msc_gray_firewall_p: Cross-level Gray paths and the specified management-to-lower-level paths must cross a Gray Firewall. The full specification also includes device placement, levels, intended-peer filtering and physical protection.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.gray_firewall_path_: An edge check supports a proof for every finite path. Separate lemmas derive packet restrictions from ordered rules. Role and address checks bind those arguments to the deployment records. The conclusion covers every clause of the accepted specification under the theorem’s explicit assumptions.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.msc_gray_addressing: Address ranges distinguish security levels. Relevant admitted traffic must connect the intended same-level Inner endpoints, with the recorded exceptions preserved.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.gray_addressing_fro: The proof combines range ownership with rules that restrict the endpoints. The common theorem covers both IP and Ethernet address views. The conclusion covers every clause of the accepted specification under the theorem’s explicit assumptions.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.msc_vpn_private_key: Every stored VPN private key is included. No modeled execution exports a protected key. When the optional access policy is selected, permitted reads belong to the owning gateway.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.vpn_private_key_con: Each modeled key operation preserves protected attributes. Induction extends that preservation to arbitrary finite action sequences. A checked translation connects the deployment events with those operations. The conclusion covers every clause of the accepted specification under the theorem’s explicit assumptions.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.msc_macsec_key_gene: The specification covers CKN length, key generation or EAP derivation, provisioning order, coverage of declared tunnels, server priorities and disabled fallback.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.macsec_key_generati: A finite record check establishes the structural conditions. The theorem combines those results with named generator, administrator and derivation facts. The conclusion covers every clause of the accepted specification under the theorem’s explicit assumptions.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.msc_transec_conditi: The chosen TRANSEC interpretation uses an active fixed-size cover sender for the applicable cases. The sender has valid sizes, a positive interval and a bounded queue.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.transec_conditions_: The finite installation check feeds a reusable state-transition proof about the configured cover sender and its scheduled operations. The conclusion covers every clause of the accepted specification under the theorem’s explicit assumptions.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.msc_outer_firewall_: The specification includes external connectivity, firewall placement for Public Internet use, firewall traversal for untrusted transport, and the appropriate internal Gray connection.
TDN.Requirements.outer_firewall_placemen: Local labels show that every edge avoiding a firewall stays on the same side. A general path proof rules out a firewall-free path between different sides. Positive connection witnesses establish the remaining placement clauses. The conclusion covers every clause of the accepted specification under the theorem’s explicit assumptions.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.msc_outer_third_par: A third-party feature must be disabled when the objective is selected. Under the threshold branch, its outgoing traffic must be blocked.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.third_party_service: Default-deny policy plus exclusion from every allow rule implies rejection under the ordered policy evaluator. The conclusion covers every clause of the accepted specification under the theorem’s explicit assumptions.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.msc_ip_header_and_m: Relevant Outer components and VPN gateways enforce the specified multicast, immediate IP-header, hop and selected IPv4-options restrictions. The documented MKA control exception retains explicit peer and framing conditions.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.ip_and_link_header_: Address and processing consistency connect the packet to the policy. Each allowing rule then supplies the necessary header restrictions. The theorem supports IP and Ethernet programs. The conclusion covers every clause of the accepted specification under the theorem’s explicit assumptions.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.msc_administrator_a: Every administrative operation has an earlier matching authentication. The person, component and active session must agree. AW credentials are individual, and selected standards require the corresponding assurances.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.administrator_authe: The reusable admission model accepts a protected operation only when a matching prerequisite exists. The theorem adds credential ownership, roster coverage and selected authority facts. The conclusion covers every clause of the accepted specification under the theorem’s explicit assumptions.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.gray_firewall_allow: Proves the complete Gray Firewall policy for a supported IPsec deployment. Recorded peers, source ranges and ordered rules establish the allowed traffic, required permissions and denial between different classifications.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.device_boundary_int: Proves the complete interface-filtering requirement from recorded device roles, directional rules, IPsec operations and physical-link observations. The assumptions identify which mechanism and service branches apply.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.outer_gray_IPsec_po: Proves the Outer encryptors’ Gray-side policy from their recorded IPsec peers, supported packet forms and ordered filtering rules. The same proof applies to different supported device inventories.
TDN.Compliance.Deployment.ForwardIngress: Requires the source address visible at the forwarding filter to belong to a range reachable through the actual receiving interface. The recorded owner and interface name identify that interface.
TDN.Compliance.Deployment.GrayForwardPer: Applies the receiving-interface source condition to the positive permission for forwarded traffic. Other filtering hooks have no extra condition from this definition.
TDN.Deployments.Perimeter_Baseline.compl: Applies the general Gray Firewall theorem to the recorded two-level baseline. Concrete checks establish every clause of the full required-firewall specification for that model.
TDN.Deployments.GrayFirewallShared.compl: Applies the same general Gray Firewall theorem to the recorded four-level network with shared Outer components. Concrete checks establish every clause of the full required-firewall specification for that model.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.MACsec_boundary_int: Derives the interface-filtering conditions for MACsec boundaries from explicit physical-interface rule checks. Physical plaintext remains observable when protection is disabled.
TDN.Zone: The interface regions represented by the architecture: Red, Gray, Black and local. Local includes device-internal interfaces such as loopback.
TDN.Compliance.Deployment.OrdinaryGray: Identifies an ordinary Gray router or switch with no encryption layer or infrastructure flag. At least one interface must be Gray, and every interface must be Gray or local.
TDN.Requirements.NamespaceAddressChecks: Checks both directions of the address mapping for every recorded device: each processing address belongs to that device, and every interface-local address is present in its processing record.
TDN.Requirements.namespace_local_address: Turns finite address checks into equality between the interface-based and processing-based local-address tests for any recorded device and address.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.msc_packet_size_con: Requires a model covering the deployment, a connection from packet states to transmitted sizes, absence of further fragmentation at the selected interfaces, complete interface-sizing records, and the applicable IPv4, IPv6 and optional Inner configuration conditions.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.complete_canonical_: Proves all five packet-sizing clauses from source encoding, recorded device and tunnel bindings, ordered native processing, emitted-byte size bounds and complete interface coverage. The selected configuration uses IPv4 MTU settings and leaves the optional Inner objective unselected.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.macsec_protection_f: Connects the configured MACsec protection parameters to the device operations. Every admitted frame-processing trace then satisfies the complete MACsec protection specification under the recorded model assumptions.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.macsec_authenticati: Connects each installed MACsec key to its recorded authentication and key-issuance events. The proof follows every modeled encryption use and checks the authentication-server placement and selected authentication method.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.inner_tunnel_no_byp: Uses checks on individual device operations to prove every admitted trace obeys the complete Inner no-bypass specification. Outgoing traffic has a matching Inner encryption event. Incoming traffic has a matching decryption of a tunnel present when that packet arrived.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.ProtectionLayerStep: Describes how one recorded packet-processing event changes the list of applied tunnel identifiers. Encryption adds an identifier, decryption removes one, and reception or transmission preserves the list.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.PendingInboundProte: An extra record used by the proof. It remembers the receiving device and the packet’s tunnel layers when the packet arrived, so later decryption can be checked against that same arrival.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.MatchingInboundDecr: The removed tunnel must be configured for the selected layer, have the current device as its receiver, and occur in the remembered arrival layers.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.DeviceInboundGateCh: Checks how every device step updates the remembered arrival record. The checks establish that transmission cannot continue while the required decryption is still pending.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.LayerOutboundLocalC: Checks the initial packet state and how every device step preserves the required outgoing protection. The checks also connect each recorded receive or transmit event to the relevant interface and configured tunnel.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.layer_events_have_n: Combines the tunnel-layer history with the remembered arrival record. A new outgoing tunnel layer requires an intervening encryption event, and transmission after a protected arrival requires matching decryption.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.IPsecIngressGateChe: Checks that IPsec reception uses matching policy and installed-SA records, routes stay on the same device, and an unauthenticated packet arriving from the external interface cannot pass the forwarding rules.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.MACsecIngressGateCh: Checks strict MACsec validation, physical-interface frame identity and the configured receiving tunnel. Those checks support the proof that accepted processing decrypts the received tunnel before transmission can continue.
TDN.Deployments.InnerTunnelNoBypass_IPse: Matches an observed ESP tunnel-mode record to the declared tunnel, installed outbound SA, owning device, local interface, peer addresses and matching IPsec policy.
Derives the Inner component’s tunnel-mode settings from the checked imported records. The whole no-bypass application uses these checks directly.

Applies the general Inner no-bypass theorem to every admitted Red source in the captured four-network IPsec configuration. The model holds installed state fixed and takes an explicit GCM implementation interface.
TDN.Deployments.InnerTunnelNoBypass_Macs: Applies the same general Inner no-bypass theorem to the two-peer MACsec model. Its Red endpoints are logical interfaces; its Gray connection uses physical MACsec frames.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.nested_layer_protec: Proves the full two-layer requirement for any supported deployment whose device operations pass the stated checks. The proof tracks named Inner and Outer tunnels through every finite execution. It derives encryption order, reverse decryption order and the destination of a successful cross-Black delivery. Key independence remains an explicit assumption.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.NestedFlowChecks: Requires checks at the starting state and at every allowed device step. Those checks bind the packet to its declared source, destination, Inner tunnel and Outer tunnel. They establish which tunnel layers must be present at Gray and Black interfaces.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.nested_flow_trace_e: Extends the initial-state and individual-step checks to every event in a finite packet execution. The same induction applies to different device counts, routes and protection mechanisms.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.outer_tunnel_no_byp: Proves the complete Outer no-bypass specification from local incoming and outgoing checks. Outer transmission requires encryption, passage after a protected arrival requires matching decryption, and non-control Gray arrivals already carry exactly one Inner layer.
TDN.Deployments.NestedProtection_Baselin: Applies the general two-layer theorem to all admitted Red requests in the recorded four-network IPsec deployment. Imported routes, filters, SAs and public CA relationships supply the checks. The result requires the named cryptographic implementation and key-independence assumptions.
TDN.Deployments.NestedProtection_Mixed.s: Applies the same general two-layer theorem to both Red networks in the recorded IPsec-Inner/MACsec-Outer deployment. The application uses the fixed manually installed associations and retains an explicit assumption that the two layers use independent keys.
Combines the full mixed-network RG-007 result with a proof that the modeled inbound and outbound bridge policies agree with the captured two-sided chain for every represented frame.
TDN.Deployments.NestedProtection_Mixed.P: Checks each supplied move in a candidate packet path. Every move must satisfy its processing-stage, route, policy, key, header and physical-link conditions. The check then continues from the resulting packet state.
TDN.Deployments.NestedProtection_Mixed.p: Proves that any move list passing the path checks is an accepted execution of the recorded device model. The argument works for lists of any finite length.
TDN.Deployments.NestedProtection_Mixed.r: Uses decide to check both imported delivery paths against the actual route, filter, key and link conditions. Each path contains 28 device operations.
TDN.Deployments.NestedProtection_Baselin: Checks a complete 44-step model execution carrying a nonempty payload through both IPsec layers to the recorded remote Red host.
TDN.Deployments.NestedProtection_Mixed.s: Checks a complete 28-step model execution from the first Red network to the second through Inner IPsec and Outer MACsec protection.
Checks the reverse 28-step model execution. Its SA, SCI and key comparisons use the records for that direction.
TDN.Certificates.WitnessTree.lookup_mem: A successful tree lookup identifies a record that occurs in the original tree. The witness follows explicit left/right choices.
TDN.Certificates.WitnessTree.checkWith_s: A passing check establishes the requested condition for every data leaf. Missing witness branches fail the check.
TDN.DataPlaneForwarding.table_driven_rou: The retained routes are exactly those selected by the original FIB for the supplied destination. Lean checks the proposed best routes, original-record indices, and all equal-priority alternatives.
TDN.PacketPolicy.table_driven_acl_certif: The chosen allow rule covers the packet class, and every earlier deny rule has a checked condition excluding that class. The result establishes the existing ordered-ACL allowance.
TDN.Requirements.Msc.gray_forward_checks: Reuses checked route selection and ACL witnesses to establish the original Gray forwarding conditions. The snapshot supplies the data and indices.
TDN.Deployments.GrayFirewallShared.route: Checks that the indexed route tree contains exactly the captured route list, in the same order.
Checks every route certificate against the complete captured route tree.
TDN.Deployments.GrayFirewallShared.acl_t: Checks that each captured Gray FORWARD policy maps to identical indexed rules for its interface and direction.
TDN.Deployments.GrayFirewallShared.Gray_: Checks all interface obligations using the verified route certificates for peer-source reachability.
Checks the forwarding allowances for every Gray interface, using indexed route and ACL witnesses.
